text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zambian press on Tuesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Nine university of Zambia students are expelled following riots over delayed allowances.
- Riot police use teargas to disperse over 400 local government workers who threaten to manhandle council officials over delayed salaries in northern Zambia.
- Cabinet approves a 10-year roads repair blueprint beginning this year which will see the country's road network revamped.
- President Frederick Chiluba sends a message of condolences to Jamaica on the death of former premier Michael Manley.
- Refugees from Zaire and Burundi refuse to live side-by-side in refugee camps in northern Zambia.
- A Zambian medical doctor in London is charged with professional misconduct for continuing to practice when he knew he was HIV positive.
- State House is opposed to a one week ultimatum local government officials have given illegal vendors to vacate the capital's city centre.
